children: India’s aviation safety regulator is undertaking operational as well as financial scrutiny of SpiceJet amid the airline’s financial difficulties, Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on Tuesday.
According to Naidu, the scrutiny through the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is aimed at ensuring that safety is not compromised.
“We do not want any lapse in safety,” he said, responding to a question on the airline’s financial position and pending funding under the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS).

The Minister said the Ministry of Civil Aviation continues to engage with SpiceJet and examine how it can facilitate matters. However, he pointed to limits on government intervention in private airlines.

“For the future, we are continuously engaging with the airline and examining how best the Ministry can facilitate matters. But these are private airlines, and there are limits to what the government can do,” he said.
Besides, Naidu said SpiceJet has received  ₹150 crore under ECLGS, while the remaining funding has to be worked out between the airline and its bank.
Asked about the disbursement of a further  ₹350 crore, the minister said the government had made the scheme available, but obtaining the funds was a matter for the company and the lender.
“The remaining amount is something the organisation and the bank have to work out. The scheme is in place; they need to obtain the funds,” he said.
Naidu did not indicate a timeline for further disbursement.
Furthermore, the minister, said the government had extended ECLGS in recognition of the difficulties airlines could face, particularly during the West Asia crisis.
“Our main priority is to ensure that passengers do not face inconvenience, that safety is not compromised at any cost and that smooth operations are sustained,” he said.
Meanwhile, responding to a separate question on market concentration, Naidu said India needs more airlines to meet growing demand.
“Given the numbers and the airports we have in the country, we should definitely have at least five airlines,” he said, reiterating his ambition for five airlines with at least 100 aircraft each.
In addition, he said the next phase of UDAN could support the entry of new airlines and help existing operators strengthen their operations.

title: SpiceJet under operational, financial scrutiny through DGCA: Minister
